annotations.text:
DIRECTION — "Ledger"

The product's whole value is that someone else vouched for the claim. So the interface borrows from records and registers: ruled rows instead of floating cards, a mono face for anything that is data (dates, IDs, status stamps), and status shown as a stamped tag rather than a coloured pill.

Type: Bricolage Grotesque (display) / Instrument Sans (text) / Martian Mono (record data).

Palette: oxblood #6E2B3C on warm oat #F9F6F0, near-black ink. Green and amber stay strictly semantic — they never appear as brand colour.
Every entry carries a status stamp — CONFIRMED / AWAITING / SELF-REPORTED. A refused or unasked entry can never render as a blank, which is how a declined claim used to pass as a confirmed one.

The register states plainly that Trajectory never contacts parents, and every recorded line is stamped with the staff name and file reference. The attestation checkbox is required before a record can be published.
Teenagers are on phones, so the record is designed at 390px too — no hamburger-hidden primary actions, 46px tap targets, and the confirmation quote stays visible rather than being truncated away.
